identity.trade: Salt and dried fish: the far south-west's salt pans and fish-racks, every wagon south of the stones smells of Saltwick.

greeting: Keep the pier clear, the nets dry and your questions short.
Smell that? That is the sea. Or the fish. Hard to say.
rumour: The tide tables are off by a quarter hour. For a week. The water is learning new habits.
A light under the water off the point moves against the current.
Wolves hate a salted track; Saltwick salts its verges where the stones are few.

opinions.eorl_hurst: Eorl is good company and better at keeping quiet.
opinions.wilda_yardley: I would trust Wilda with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Dawn tide. The boats are out.

dialogue.aside: Tell me everything. No, truly. I will not ask twice. I will ask three times.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
Tide waits for nobody, and neither does a net.
rumour: The fishers come in at dawn and drink till noon. Their wives come at one.
Somebody paid in old coin last night. Very old. Nobody knew the king on it.
The shoals went deep a month early. The old fishers say the cold comes from below.
Whatever you hear about Saltwick, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.wat_stoker: I would trust Wat with a purse. A small one.

time.evening: Boats are in. The catch is salted. Supper is fish.

dialogue.aside: Friend, you know I will not change my mind. Ask anyway. I enjoy refusing you.

greeting: Bring iron or bring coin. Preferably iron.
Saltwick is salt pans and fisheries. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Hooks, gaffs and anchors. If it holds a boat, I forged it.
Plough blades sell slow and spear heads sell fast. I do not like what that says.
A boy swore he saw a ship at the mouth of the bay with no mast and no crew. The tide took it.

opinions.garth_carver: Garth undercuts me. I forgive Garth. Mostly.

time.night: Night tide. Quiet water, loud thoughts.

dialogue.aside: Look what the wind dragged in. Sit. Do not touch the pie.

greeting: Take your time. Touch nothing you cannot afford.
Welcome to Saltwick. Mind the Saltwick Salt Works. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Hooks, floats and twine. If it is thin and sharp, it is a bestseller.
Sold three lanterns today. People are afraid of the dark again.
A boat came back empty with its sail torn, as if something had pulled at it.
The Saltwick Salt Works was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.bede_farrow: Bede undercuts me. I forgive Bede. Mostly.

time.rain: Rain on the water. The fish bite better and so do the midges.

dialogue.aside: What did you see on the road? Tell me every bit. I will keep the details.

greeting: Loaf, bun, or the heel nobody wants? The heel is free.
Strangers in Saltwick get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: A sack of flour came in short, twice. The miller swears by his scales.
A seal followed my boat for a mile and spoke. I did not answer.
A pinch of salt on the doorstep keeps small dark things out, say Saltwick folk.

opinions.sander_tolliver: Sander and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

time.morning: Dawn tide. The boats are out.

dialogue.aside: You know me. You know my work. I will not insult either by modesty.

greeting: Tell me where it hurts. Then tell me what you did before it hurt.
Saltwick is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Fever in two households. Nothing the stones can mend.
Tides follow the moon, they say. Ours follow something else. The old men have stopped betting.

opinions.jory_wherry: Jory is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.evening: Boats are in. The catch is salted. Supper is fish.

dialogue.aside: Take your time, friend. I am in no hurry. I am, in fact, very good at waiting.

greeting: State your business and keep your hands where I can see them.
You will hear Saltwick before you see it. Ask at the Saltwick Salt Works.
rumour: Fewer travellers on the road, more strange footprints at the verge. I count both.
The gulls leave the harbour every evening in a line. They did not use to.
The last salt caravan never made it past the Emberfall Roadhouse.

opinions.eda_ledger: Eda works hard and talks harder.
opinions.vera_fletcher: Vera knows the trade. I will say that for Vera.

time.night: Night tide. Quiet water, loud thoughts.

dialogue.aside: Knock on wood, friend. Now touch iron. There. Safe, for a while.

greeting: Move along. Or stay, but stay quiet.
First time in Saltwick? The Saltwick Salt Works is the place to start.
rumour: A stone by the gate flickered at midnight. I wrote it down. Nobody reads it.
A net came up with a coil of old chain in it, links as long as a forearm. We put it back.
Ask anyone in Saltwick about the Saltwick Salt Works. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.vera_fletcher: Vera works hard and talks harder.

dialogue.aside: Forgive me. It has been a long week and a longer day. Still, it is good to see you.

greeting: Evening. Stones are lit, gate is shut, I am cold.
Folk come to Saltwick for salt pans and fisheries. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: Cold on the wall these nights. Colder than the season has a right to be.
Fish tasted of iron last week. Not bad. Not right.

greeting: You are somebody's grandchild. I can tell by the walk.
If it floats, I have fished from it. If it sank, I have fished it up.
rumour: When I was young the stones sang at dusk. Now they hum, like someone ill.
The tide marks on the pier are wrong. Higher than last year, higher than the old stone.
The Saltwick Salt Works drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.lowen_graye: Lowen lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.evening: Boats are in. The catch is salted. Supper is fish.

dialogue.aside: A friend is a rare coin. I have spent worse.

greeting: Come closer. My ears are old and your voice is young.
The Saltwick Salt Works is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: The old stones had names. Nobody writes them down. Nobody asks me.
Ask in Saltwick who built the Saltwick Salt Works and you will get a different name each time.

opinions.rafe_crowther: Rafe keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.wendel_rawlin: Wendel lives next door and hears everything I do.

dialogue.aside: Come in, sit, eat. I will hear no argument.

greeting: A pinch of this keeps meat for a month. A pinch of me keeps you out of my pans.
rumour: A wagon left with salt and came back without the driver. The mule knew the road.
The Saltwick Salt Works has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

rumour: Nets come back torn in places no fish reaches.
Saltwick lives by salt pans and fisheries. When that fails, so do we.

dialogue.aside: You look rough. Eat something. That is not advice, it is an order.

greeting: Salt keeps. People, less so.
rumour: The brine pans froze in the night, in autumn. I skimmed ice off the salt in September.
Every few years Saltwick has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

rumour: Wolves tracked a cart for two miles last week. I counted the miles, not the wolves.
If trade slows, Saltwick feels it first. If it speeds up, Saltwick feels it last.

rumour: Found a net cut clean, not torn. Cut.
When Saltwick is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.
